script: Update a position. Update a position when the role changes: its name, a reclassification with a new job code, its assignment category, its work unit, for example when expenses are tracked differently, or its work location. Some changes reach the incumbent's assignment automatically once approved. Others don't, so plan a second transaction for those.
Open the position. Go to Our Workforce, then Show More, then Positions, under Workforce Structures. Search for the position, and open it.
Choose Update, and enter the effective date: the date the change takes effect. For example, September first for a reclassification.

Pick the action reason that matches the change. Updates have more reasons than new positions, for example a reclassification to a higher range, an assignment category change, or a work unit or location change. The reason drives reporting.

Change the fields that changed. For a reclassification, enter the new six-digit job code from Compensation's reclass memo, the new name, and the new assignment category if it changed. Fix anything else that's wrong while you're there, such as headcount type.
Attach the reclass memo, add comments, and submit. Approval follows the same path as a new position.

After approval, update the incumbent's assignment for what didn't flow. Person type, location, working hours, and hourly salary don't sync from the position. Open the employee's Employment Info, and use Change Assignment to update them, and the business title.

Two things to remember. Position changes never reach an existing requisition; it keeps the position as it was when submitted. And reclassifications need Compensation's reclass memo before you update the position.
